title: Health Education - Laws and Policies
before:
Laws & Policies for Health Education

There are many laws, statutes, rules, and policies that govern and guide Maine's education system. A quality health education curriculum will align to and incorporate related laws and policies. The following laws and policies are relevant to health education.

Maine Health Education Regulations for the Implementation of Maine Learning Results

  • Elementary course of study
  • Junior high or middle school course of study
  • Secondary schools general requirements
  • System of learning results established

Content Area Specific Laws & Policies

Health Education has ten content areas, each with its own affiliated laws, statutes, and policies.

Community Health

Maine Center for Disease Control and Prevention — search this site for laws on specific health issues.

Consumer Health

Consumer Product Safety Commission — laws, regulations, and information to protect the public against unreasonable risks of injuries and deaths associated with consumer products.

Environmental Health

Maine Environmental Health Laws — search this site for laws on specific environmental health issues.

Family Life

Maine Comprehensive Family Life Education Statute — provides a definition of Comprehensive Family Life Education.

Nutritional Health

Federal Wellness Policy — law requiring the establishment of a local wellness policy by schools.

Personal Health, Including Mental & Emotional Health
  • Maine Bullying Prevention Laws — laws and specific resources for bullying prevention.
  • Maine Concussion Law — laws and specific resources for concussion management.
Prevention & Control of Disease & Disorders

Maine Center for Disease Control and Prevention — search this site for laws on specific diseases and disorders.

Substance Use & Abuse

Maine Liquor Laws — view Maine laws related to liquor.

Safety & Accident Prevention
  • Child Sexual Abuse Prevention and Response — the Maine Department of Education Model Policy as directed by Maine law Public Law 2015, Ch. 292. Supporting materials can be found at the Children's Safety Partnership.
  • FAQ Sheet: Maine Suicide Prevention and Awareness Education Law — assists schools in clarifying the law, answering questions related to the trainings, and providing links to the law and training sites.
  • Rules to Support Maine's Suicide Awareness and Prevention Law for Schools — Chapter 38 rule establishes state standards and procedures for suicide prevention awareness education for all school personnel and suicide prevention and intervention training.
  • Maine Bullying Prevention Laws — laws and specific resources for bullying prevention.
  • Maine Bicycle and Pedestrian Safety Laws — laws specific to bicycle and pedestrian safety in Maine.
  • Maine Concussion Law — laws and specific resources for concussion management.

notes: 2 section headers — too few for a contents list.

decisions.label: Give the cards the width their content needs
decisions.why: 1 row holds two cards of very different weight in equal halves, and cards in a row are the same height — so the short one is stretched and the difference shows as empty space. 7.1× — 1165 characters beside 163. Only the column widths change.

decisions.label: Drop the dash once the link is set apart
decisions.why: 8 of those items separate the link from its description with a dash. The link is now set in the display face at a larger size with a chevron after it, so the dash marks a boundary that is already unmistakable. Only the separator is removed — no word changes.

decisions.label: Separate a link from its description
decisions.why: 8 list items open with a link and then explain it, all at the same weight — so the thing you can click is no easier to find than the sentence about it. The link becomes the item and the explanation sits under it.

decisions.label: Set a link apart from its description in a paragraph
decisions.why: 7 paragraphs open with a link and then describe it, separated by a dash — the same shape the list items above use, written as a paragraph, and until now it was the one place that got no treatment at all. The link takes the display face and a chevron, the description sits under it at body size, and the dash goes because the treatment has taken over its job. No word changes.

decisions.label: Use this paragraph as the page description
decisions.why: It is the page’s own opening paragraph, moved into the banner rather than rewritten.
decisions.value: There are many laws, statutes, rules, and policies that govern and guide Maine's education system. A quality health education curriculum will align to and incorporate related laws and policies. The following laws and policies are relevant to health education.

decisions.label: Bring every heading up to h3 or above
decisions.why: 1 heading sat at h4 or deeper inside a card, a callout, a contact block or an accordion panel — components the outline walk leaves alone because they label a thing rather than a section. A reader using a screen reader still hears the level, so a fourth-level title inside a page that only goes to three is announced as belonging to a level that does not exist. Each is styled by its class and its position rather than its number, so nothing changes on screen.

decisions.label: Start a description with a capital
decisions.why: 7 descriptions begin with a small letter, because they used to run on from the link after a dash. The dash is gone and the link now sits above in its own face, so each description opens a line of its own. One character changes and only ever the first.
